Azure Government note: Python/R visuals are Verify for Gov. Validate Desktop configuration, approved packages, Service support, and customer policy before delivery.

When approved for use:
1. Confirm the approved Python or R runtime and package list with the tenant/security team — Desktop requires a local runtime install, and the Service requires an admin-enabled tenant setting plus (for scheduled refresh) a personal gateway.
2. Create a simple visual (for example, a Matplotlib or ggplot2 chart) using only non-sensitive workshop data such as Sales Amount by Product Category.
3. Document every package dependency by name and version so it can be reviewed for tenant approval.
4. Review Service limitations: Python/R visuals do not render in the Service unless the tenant setting is enabled, and scheduled refresh requires a gateway with the matching runtime installed.

Gov-safe alternate path: use native Power BI visuals (bar/line/scatter/table) or a precomputed Power Query column/table instead of a code-based visual. Native visuals render everywhere without an approved-runtime dependency.

Deliverable for this exercise: a one-paragraph write-up naming (a) the specific chart you would build, (b) its package dependencies, and (c) the native-visual fallback you would use if Python/R is not approved for your tenant.
